_comment: Pre-specified series list. Selection rationale was written BEFORE any forecaster was fitted or scored. Selection criteria: (1) business relevance, (2) breadth across domains and across seasonally-adjusted (SA) vs not-seasonally-adjusted (NSA) forms, (3) complete monthly coverage 1992-01..2025-09 (405 observations, verified by counts only). Series are NOT independent (e.g. SA/NSA twins, total vs component); this is a threat to validity listed in docs/protocol.md.

window.end_rationale: The last month before the Oct-Nov 2025 US data-collection gap, which leaves a missing October 2025 value in the CPI series. Using one common end date avoids interpolating actuals.

fred.title: Advance Retail Sales: Retail Trade and Food Services (NSA)
fred.reason: Headline consumer-demand series used in retail and finance forecasting; strong calendar seasonality (December peak).

fred.title: Advance Retail Sales: Retail Trade and Food Services (SA)
fred.reason: Seasonally adjusted twin of the headline series; lets us contrast seasonal vs de-seasonalised behaviour (relevant to H4).

fred.title: Retail Sales: Motor Vehicle and Parts Dealers (NSA)
fred.reason: Largest durable-goods retail category; cyclical with moderate seasonality.

fred.title: Retail Sales: Grocery Stores (NSA)
fred.reason: Staple-goods category with stable level and stable seasonality (candidate for H4: seasonal-naive-friendly).

fred.title: Retail Sales: Clothing and Clothing Accessories Stores (NSA)
fred.reason: Highly seasonal discretionary category with a large pandemic shock.

fred.title: Retail Sales: Nonstore Retailers (NSA)
fred.reason: E-commerce proxy with strong trend and evolving seasonality (hard for seasonal-naive).

fred.title: Retail Sales: Building Materials and Garden Equipment and Supplies Dealers (NSA)
fred.reason: Weather-driven seasonality tied to housing activity.

fred.title: Retail Sales: Food Services and Drinking Places (NSA)
fred.reason: Services-like category with a very large 2020 collapse and recovery.

fred.title: Retail Sales: Gasoline Stations (NSA)
fred.reason: Price-driven (energy) volatility on top of seasonality.

fred.title: Retail Sales: Furniture and Home Furnishings Stores (NSA)
fred.reason: Housing-linked discretionary category with moderate seasonality.

fred.title: Industrial Production: Total Index (SA)
fred.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
fred.reason: Standard real-activity indicator; smooth, trending, not seasonal.

fred.title: Industrial Production: Manufacturing (SA)
fred.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
fred.reason: Manufacturing component, relevant to supply-chain and operations forecasting.

fred.title: Industrial Production: Total Index (NSA)
fred.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
fred.reason: Raw, un-adjusted total index; seasonal pattern (summer shutdowns) present.

fred.title: Industrial Production: Electric Power Generation, Transmission and Distribution (NSA)
fred.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
fred.reason: Electricity output series (energy-analytics relevance); strong temperature-driven seasonality, stable level.

fred.title: Industrial Production: Motor Vehicles and Parts (NSA)
fred.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
fred.reason: Volatile durable-goods manufacturing series with annual shutdown seasonality.

fred.title: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items (NSA)
fred.reason: Headline inflation index; trending with weak seasonality; central to finance forecasting.

fred.title: CPI for All Urban Consumers: All Items Less Food and Energy (SA)
fred.reason: Core inflation; smooth trend, no seasonality.

fred.title: CPI-U: Food at Home (NSA)
fred.reason: Staple price component with weak seasonality and a 2021-2023 shock.

fred.title: CPI-U: Rent of Primary Residence (NSA)
fred.reason: Very smooth, persistent price series (random-walk-with-drift territory).

fred.title: CPI-U: Gasoline, All Types (NSA)
fred.reason: Highly volatile commodity-driven price series.

fred.title: CPI-U: Electricity (NSA)
fred.reason: Utility price series (energy analytics); seasonal tariff pattern.

fred.title: New Privately-Owned Housing Units Started: Total Units (SA)
fred.source: U.S. Census Bureau and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
fred.reason: Housing-construction cycle indicator; noisy.

fred.title: New Privately-Owned Housing Units Started: Total Units (NSA)
fred.source: U.S. Census Bureau and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
fred.reason: Raw twin of HOUST with strong weather seasonality.

fred.title: New Privately-Owned Housing Units Authorized in Permit-Issuing Places: Total Units (SA)
fred.source: U.S. Census Bureau and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
fred.reason: Leading housing indicator, smoother than starts.

fred.title: Total Vehicle Sales (SA, millions of units, annual rate)
fred.reason: Auto-sector demand (auto-sales relevance); cyclical with supply shocks.

fred.title: Total Vehicle Sales (NSA, thousands of units)
fred.reason: Raw twin of TOTALSA with strong seasonality.

fred.title: All Employees, Total Nonfarm (NSA)
fred.reason: Large, smooth level series with mild seasonality and a one-month 2020 collapse.

fred.title: Unemployment Rate (NSA)
fred.reason: A rate (bounded, mean-reverting) rather than a level, adding a different series shape.

fred.title: Vehicle Miles Traveled (NSA)
fred.reason: Mobility/activity series with strong seasonality and a pandemic shock; fuel-demand relevance.

fred.title: M2 Money Stock (SA)
fred.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
fred.reason: Finance-flavoured, smooth, strongly trending series with no seasonality; a stress test for trend handling.

electricity.aggregation: sum of hourly values per calendar day (UTC-naive timestamps as given)
electricity.selection_rule: eligible = series with at most 3 zero hourly values in the whole span (the zeros that occur at the March clock-change hour in each of the 3 years are tolerated) and no missing values; take 30 eligible series at evenly spaced positions floor(i * n_eligible / 30), i = 0..29, in the file's original order
